gap: No result ChatGPT got states, in one place, each candidate's maker-store price on 2026-11-26 next to how many added screens each 15-inch Air chip drives: the one-screen picks ($143.99 Fold 15.6, $247.99 Duex Float 2 Pro at mobilepixels.us) fall within Apple's one-external-display limit for the M2 and M3, while the two-screen sets ($199.99 FOPO S7, $299.99 FOPO S10, $407.99 Trio 3 Pro) exceed it and fit Apple's lid-open limit only on the M4 and M5.
standout_why: Compared against Macworld (cited), thisUSB (cited), Dealectric's best-laptop-screen-extender (cited, ours) and WorkCocoon's MacBook Air page. Each has part of it. thisUSB gives the chip rule (M1/M2 one, M3 two lid closed, M4/M5 two lid open) but no prices and no Duex, Trio or FOPO. Macworld gives prices and weights (Float 2 Pro 2.9 lb, Trio 3 Pro 4.13 lb) but no MacBook Air statement; its only limit note covers plain M1/M2 Macs and the MacBook Neo. Our own cited page already pairs the chip rule with 11-21 prices for the Trio, Duex Max DS, Float 2 Pro and FOPO S7. WorkCocoon has no prices, weights or chip limits. What none has: the 15-inch Air's own figures (3.3 lb, 13.40 in wide, 224 ppi, per Apple) set against each candidate, the M5 row from Apple's spec page, and the maker price for ChatGPT's two non-partner picks (ASUS lists none; espresso $699).
decides: It confirms rather than changes the pick. On an M2 or M3 Air the page should rank one-screen models first. Apple's pages give those chips one external display with the lid open, and all three two-screen sets priced here list as driver-free on the native path. Reading that as 'only one of their two screens lights without a driver' is my inference from the two facts, not a maker statement. Among one-screen picks, the Duex Float 2 Pro at $247.99 is the only attached or stacked model whose maker fit range (15–16 in, per our record) names the Air's size and whose 2560×1600 panel is closest to the Air's 224 ppi. Its cost is weight: 2.9 lb (Macworld) on a 3.3 lb laptop. The Duex Max DS stays the side-slide pick, but its price was not re-read today (store returned 429). ChatGPT's $175.99 Walmart card sits below the maker's $215.99 from 11-21, so the page must not claim a lowest price. On an M4 or M5 Air the Trio 3 Pro at $407.99 is the two-screen pick by Apple's two-display spec; Macworld weighs it at 4.13 lb, more than the Air itself. The two rival picks lose on price facts: ASUS shows no store price for the MB16ACV (1080p), and the espresso Pro 15 is $699 at its maker, about 2.8 times the Float 2 Pro.

findings.label: 15-inch MacBook Air M2 (2023): external displays
findings.value: One external display, up to 6K at 60 Hz, native DisplayPort over USB-C; two Thunderbolt / USB 4 ports
findings.note: Apple's Display Support section. Any second added screen on this chip needs a display driver (DisplayLink or the maker's own).

findings.label: 15-inch MacBook Air M3 (2024): external displays
findings.value: One external display up to 6K at 60 Hz with the lid open; 'Close the MacBook Air lid to use a second external display with up to 5K resolution at 60Hz'
findings.note: An attached two-screen extender needs the lid open, so the M3 is in the one-screen group for this category.

findings.label: 15-inch MacBook Air M4 (2025): external displays
findings.value: Up to two external displays, up to 6K at 60 Hz, alongside the built-in display; native DisplayPort 1.4 over USB-C; two Thunderbolt 4 ports
findings.note: Two screens with one cable each use both Thunderbolt ports; MagSafe remains for charging.

findings.label: 15-inch MacBook Air M5 (2026): external displays
findings.value: Up to two external displays (two up to 6K at 60 Hz or 4K at 144 Hz) with the built-in display at full resolution; 'Supports up to two external displays over a single Thunderbolt port'
findings.note: Apple's External Display Support section.
